(i) real interest rates depend significantly upon current debt, (ii) the effect of debt on interest rates depends upon foreign interest rates, and (iii) the asymmetry of the effect of foreign interest rates upon domestic interest rates is still present.

the level of government debt is a key determinant of real interest rates, that this relationship has not disappeared with financial integration, but that the strength of the relationship has been diluted by financial integration.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between debt and interest rates.
the effect of debt on interest rates.
the effect on interest rates of changes in debt and other macroeconomic variables, with particular emphasis upon the effect of debt and the effect of US and European interest rates upon each other.

debt matters for interest rates but the evidence is not as conclusive as it might be.

the effect of government debt on interest rates is significant, but not large, in the U.S. and in Europe, and that the effect of U.S. interest rates on European rates is also significant but not large.
debt and interest rates are linked, but the links are not simple, and are not always in the direction one might have expected.

the effects of government debt on interest rates have been much weaker than previously thought, and that the effects of US interest rates have been stronger.

the effect of debt on interest rates is a key issue for the future of the euro area, especially in the context of the sovereign debt crisis.
